items.sentence: Usually made from hardwood, bamboo, or food-grade plastic, its broad, rigid face withstands repeated knife contact.
Some versions have a shallow perimeter channel that catches juices released by meat or ripe produce.
A nonslip underside or rubber feet help keep the flat platform stable on a countertop.
Thick wooden models may be built from edge-grain or end-grain strips joined together.
During washing, plastic surfaces can generally go in a dishwasher, while many wooden ones require hand cleaning and prompt drying.
A cook can rotate or reposition it to expose an unused area as food preparation continues.
After contact with raw meat, the surface is washed and sanitized before another ingredient is prepared.
Knife blades strike and slide across it, leaving shallow marks that accumulate with repeated use.
In home kitchens, it is often placed beside the sink or stove before ingredients are chopped.
Commercial kitchens may assign separate colored surfaces to different food groups to reduce cross-contamination.
During outdoor picnics, a lightweight plastic version can provide a clean preparation area on a folding table.
Butcher counters use thick wooden surfaces for breaking down large cuts, often with sturdy supports.
It shields countertops from blade scratches and helps prevent food juices from reaching the work surface.
Its stable plane gives cooks a controlled place to slice, dice, mince, or portion ingredients.
By providing a washable barrier, it makes cleanup after food preparation easier.
Its replaceable surface absorbs the wear of chopping, sparing more expensive kitchen counters from damage.
